variants.title: Charging a capacitor: 1000, 2200 and 4700 µF with a 100 Ω-step box
variants.sample: Electrolytics 1000 / 2200 / 4700 µF, box in 100 Ω steps
variants.method: Large capacitors with a box in 100 Ω steps: ten times the capacitance, a tenth of the resistance
variants.note: 1000, 2200 and 4700 are E6 preferred values. RC is still a few seconds because R is ten times smaller and C ten times larger.

source.title: IEC 60063: preferred number series (E6: 10, 15, 22, 33, 47, 68)
source.note: Aluminium electrolytic capacitors are sold in E6 values with ±20 % tolerance (IEC 60384-4).

variants.title: Charging a capacitor: 10, 22 and 47 µF with a 10 kΩ-step box
variants.sample: Electrolytics 10 / 22 / 47 µF, box in 10 kΩ steps
variants.method: Small capacitors with large resistances (100-200 kΩ)
variants.note: With R of a hundred kilo-ohms a moving-coil voltmeter would draw a noticeable share of the current; this lab's voltmeter is taken as ideal (like a 10 MΩ digital meter).

source.title: IEC 60063: preferred number series (E6: 10, 15, 22, 33, 47, 68)
source.note: Aluminium electrolytic capacitors are sold in E6 values with ±20 % tolerance (IEC 60384-4).

variants.title: Charging a capacitor: 330, 470 and 680 µF
variants.method: Three neighbouring E6 values, so the time constants are close together
variants.note: Neighbouring E6 values differ by about 1.5 times; the measured τ must follow RC just as closely.

source.title: IEC 60063: preferred number series (E6: 10, 15, 22, 33, 47, 68)

variants.title: RC charging: find the capacitance of an unknown capacitor X
variants.method: τ for several known R; C = slope of τ against R
variants.unknown: the capacitance C of capacitor X
variants.note: A generic capacitor whose marking is covered: its value is found only from the charging time.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XII, Ch 2 Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
source.note: Generic unknown capacitor; 330 µF is an E6 value (IEC 60063).

variants.title: RC charging: find the capacitance of a second unknown capacitor Y
variants.method: τ for several known R; C = slope of τ against R
variants.unknown: the capacitance C of capacitor Y
variants.note: A generic capacitor whose marking is covered, about twice the size of X.

source.title: NCERT Physics Part I, Class XII, Ch 2 Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance

variants.title: RC charging: the real value of a capacitor marked 470 µF
variants.method: τ for several known R; C = slope of τ against R, compared with the marking
variants.unknown: the real capacitance of the 470 µF capacitor
variants.note: Electrolytic capacitors are made to ±20 %: anything from 376 to 564 µF meets this marking. Find out where this one lies.

source.title: IEC 60384-4: aluminium electrolytic capacitors, tolerance code M = ±20 %
source.note: The capacitor in this lab has a real value inside the tolerance band; it is an example, not a measured part.

variants.title: RC charging: the real value of a capacitor marked 1000 µF
variants.method: τ for several known R; C = slope of τ against R, compared with the marking
variants.unknown: the real capacitance of the 1000 µF capacitor
variants.note: Electrolytic capacitors are made to ±20 %: anything from 800 to 1200 µF meets this marking. Its time constants are long, so be patient at the 63 % mark.
